text.p: Guinea-Bissau President Joao Bernardo Vieira issued a decree on Monday night dissolving the government led by Prime Minister Manuel Saturnino da Costa, the Portuguese news agency Lusa said.

Lusa, reporting from the West African state's capital Bissau, said Vieira took the decision because of a "grave political crisis" which was jeopardising the normal operations of state institutions. The agency gave no details of the crisis.

It said Da Costa's government would remain in office pending the appointment of a new executive but did not say when the new government would be sworn in. Lusa did not name any members of the new government.
Da Costa's government took office in November 1994.
Guinea-Bissau, a former Portuguese colony, is one of the world's poorest countries.
